lines: -# Emit a dev-mode diagnostic when a self-referential effect re-renders past a threshold

-A `` compiles to a `_let("n/1", ...)` signal that invokes the `_script` effect, whose body calls the setter again: `_let`'s non-rendering branch fires `schedule()` + `queueRender` on every value change with no per-scope update counter, `_script` is a bare `queueEffect` with no dedupe, and `run()` in `dom/queue.ts` drains renders then effects with no depth tracking. Mounted in jsdom the effect runs ~124 times per second (the `queueMicrotask`->`requestAnimationFrame`->`MessageChannel` pacing in `dom/schedule.ts` yields ~2 passes per frame), `n` grows unbounded and the console stays silent; a terminating variant (`if (n < 3) n = n + 1`) settles at `n = 3`, showing each self-write is a full render+effect pass. Writing state from an effect is user error (derive with ``), so the gap is the diagnostic React and Solid provide. Add a `MARKO_DEBUG`-only update-depth guard in `run()`/`queueRender` that throws after N self-perpetuating passes on the same scope+signal.
-# Keep a source position and a stack on an `Unable to serialize` error

-`throwUnserializable` appends `:line:column` only when the failing binding has a `root.loc`, so any value spelled off `input` names the bare file and no position — `packages/runtime-tags/src/__tests__/fixtures/component-attrs-import-value` reports `…/counter.marko` while `unserializable-warning` reports `…/template.marko:2:10` for the same class of failure. The line right after builds the error and sets `err.stack = undefined`, discarding the only other locator, so under `@marko/run` dev the error page ships `{"message":…,"stack":"","frame":""}` and renders an empty `<pre>`: the browser overlay is one sentence with no file position, no frame and no stack, which is what turns a serialization failure into a bisection hunt. The translator already emits a per-var loc in the `writeScope` debug object and just leaves it off `input`-rooted references (`input.option` becomes `["input.option"]` with no second element), so the position of the read is available to attach. Either carry that loc through, or keep a trimmed stack so the dev server can build a frame; either satisfies the requirement, which is that the error reaches the overlay carrying at least one locator.

-Check: `cat packages/runtime-tags/src/__tests__/fixtures/{unserializable-warning,component-attrs-import-value}/__snapshots__/ssr.error.debug.txt` — only the first carries `:2:10`; both should carry a position. Under `marko-run dev`, the same failure serves an error payload whose `stack` and `frame` are both `""`; expect a non-empty `frame` or a `stack` the dev server can build one from.
-# Diagnose a `client`/`server` binding read during render

-A `client`-scoped module binding is `undefined` on the other platform, and reading one while rendering fails without ever mentioning Marko. `client const CHART = { name: "x" };` with `
${CHART.name}
` throws a bare `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` during SSR — no template, no tag, no hint that `CHART` is platform-scoped — while the plain `${CHART}` form renders empty and reports nothing at all. The cheatsheet warns about the call shape (`is not a function`), which covers only one of the three ways this lands. The translator already knows which bindings a `client`/`server` block declares and which expressions run during render, so it can name the binding and the reason. -# Warn in MARKO_DEBUG when a page carries resume data the DOM runtime never initialized

-A client bundle built from a plain `output: "dom"` compile never becomes interactive, with zero diagnostics: the SSR page ships correct HTML plus the inline bootstrap that parks resume payloads on `self[runtimeId]`, and nothing consumes them, because `init()` is emitted only by the compiler's entry builder, reached only via `entry: "page"` — which `packages/runtime-tags/src/translator/visitors/program/index.ts` rejects with ``The "entry" option requires the `linkAssets` compiler option to be configured`` — or the deprecated `output: "hydrate"`. No `linkAssets` implementation ships outside this repo's own test bundler, so anyone integrating Marko 6 with their own bundler lands here, and nothing signals it anywhere on the path: `init` carries no JSDoc, no repo-owned doc names it, `packages/compiler/config.d.ts` declares `entry?: EntryKind` with no comment at all, and its `output` deprecation note steers readers from `"hydrate"` to `output: "dom", entry: "page"` without mentioning that the second throws without `linkAssets`. Add a `MARKO_DEBUG`-guarded check that, at document `load`, walks the render entries on `self[DEFAULT_RUNTIME_ID]` and warns once when any has pending resume data and was never initialized, matching the precedent `readyFailed` sets in this same file for the analogous "server-rendered content cannot become interactive" failure so production compiles no call site; a non-default `runtimeId` yields a false negative rather than a false positive, a static SSR page emits no bootstrap at all, and `template.mount()` never writes `self[runtimeId]`, so the two legitimately non-interactive shapes cannot trigger it. Pair it with JSDoc on `init`/`initEmbedded` and a `linkAssets`-required note on `entry` in `packages/compiler/config.d.ts`.

-Check: Compile a `counter.marko` (`<let/count=0/>` plus `<button onClick() { count++ }>Count: ${count}</button>`) from the same source path twice, with `pnpm run compile -- -o dom -d` and `-o html -d`, so the registry ids match; the dom output contains no `init` call. Bundle the dom output as an IIFE with `var MARKO_DEBUG = true;` prepended, load it as an inline script after the rendered SSR HTML in jsdom with `runScripts: "dangerously"`, and dispatch a click: the text stays `Count: 0`, the console is empty, and `window.M._.r` still holds its resume entries. The same bundle plus `import { init } from "@marko/runtime-tags/debug/dom"; init();` counts up and drains `M._.r`.
-# Warn in MARKO_DEBUG when an update is dropped into an already-caught `<try>`

-Once `@catch` renders, `renderCatch` destroys the `<try>`'s content branch and its subscriptions, so assigning a fresh promise to the awaited value is dropped: the DOM stays frozen on the error branch while surrounding state keeps updating. The identical assignment in the identical template updates normally when no error occurred, so a retry button looks correct, runs its handler, resolves its fetch, bumps its own state — and simply never re-renders, with nothing logged, thrown, or type-checked; the closure's target scope set is empty, so the update reaches nobody. The only statements of the rule are an internal comment above `renderCatch` and one line in `packages/runtime-tags/cheatsheet.md`, neither of which a developer debugging a frozen UI reaches (markojs.com's core-tag reference omits the recovery semantics entirely, and that page lives in the website repo). The signal that fires at the moment of loss is a `MARKO_DEBUG`-only diagnostic on the dropped path: mark the owner scope in `renderCatch` when a catch destroys a content branch, and in `_closure` (`src/dom/signals.ts`), when a signal fires with no live target scopes on a marked owner, `console.error` that `@catch` cannot recover in place and the boundary must be re-rendered (e.g. by bumping a key on a wrapping `<for>`) — the same shape as the existing debug-only `_global_read` diagnostic. Back it with a one-line JSDoc on `Input.catch` in the shipped `packages/runtime-tags/tags/try.d.marko` stub, which `translator/core/try.ts` points `<try>`'s types at and which `.d.marko` tooling treats as TS, so the rule also surfaces on hover while the `@catch` is being written.
